> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/qa/scenarios/README.md`, `packages/qa/scenarios/src/runner/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **23** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **226** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e159102d03db8ad8bd1d7a6962300000f1bece97` — the merge of head `fb1d76f7d24678c01304f573d97d45a046409bf7` into base `455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e159102d03db8ad8bd1d7a6962300000f1bece97 && git checkout e159102d03db8ad8bd1d7a6962300000f1bece97
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 fb1d76f7d24678c01304f573d97d45a046409bf7 && git checkout -B drift-repro 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3 && git merge --no-ff fb1d76f7d24678c01304f573d97d45a046409bf7

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 455229e7aebae2fe91ada77736377fe145defba3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `fb1d76f7d24678c01304f573d97d45a046409bf7`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #31159 (body, triage 6709176909, claim 6712196415, os-dev-report 6712807610), PR #31265 (body, 15-file list, net diff `origin/main...fb1d76f7`), and the 45 check-runs on the head. Read-only: the diff was read from the fetched objects, nothing built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept set of `makeDriver`** (`src/runner/cli.ts`): `claude` (unchanged), `codex`, `external:COMMAND`, `recorded:FILE`. Refused: `external:` with an empty or blank command (`needs a command`, from `parseExternalCommand`); `codex` with `--author-max-turns` or `--ask-max-turns` (`has/have no equivalent in the Codex CLI`); `recorded:` with any live flag (unchanged); every other name, with the message now listing all four. The default `claude` path is unchanged in substance: `runCli` became `runTurnProcess` in `drivers/process.ts` with the same body and the same `subscriptionOnlyEnv()` child environment.
- **External contract, README versus implementation** (`README.md` "Other agent tools" against `drivers/external.ts`): they agree on every point I compared — one process per call; `info` once in the constructor before any card, refused on non-zero exit, prose or a missing binary; `author` runs in `cwd`, `ask` in the config file's directory; strict `ExternalTurnSchema` (unknown key refused); exit 0 with the declared shape is the turn; non-zero exit, signal or the runner's timeout is `no-result(exit N | signal S)` via `noResult`; other stdout is `invalid-output(why)` with `isError`; `limits.timeoutMs` is `--author-timeout` (default 60 min from `DEFAULT_AUTHOR_TIMEOUT_MIN`) or 5 min for `ask`, SIGTERM at the deadline; stderr tail 2,000 characters; `maxTurns` and `model` carried in `limits` and on `meta.process`; the four billing variables deleted from the child environment. `authorNotMeasured` in `orchestrate.ts` turns every failed authoring turn into a not-measured Build half, so "never an empty pass" holds. Two small documentation gaps, neither a contract break: the README does not state the `info` name grammar (`ExternalInfoSchema` regex: letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`) nor the 30 s `info` timeout (`infoTimeoutMs`).
- **Exports reachable through `./runner`** (`src/runner/index.ts` now `export *` from `drivers/codex.js` and `drivers/external.js`; `drivers/process.ts` not re-exported, as the PR says): comparing the exported names of `driver.ts`, `transcript.ts`, `runner/index.ts` and `export/index.ts` on `origin/main` against the head yields no name present on main and absent at the head. The 89 lines deleted from `driver.ts` were the module-private `CliRun`, `STDERR_TAIL`, `runCli` and `noResult`; the 12 from `transcript.ts` the private `resultText` (now `contentText` in process.ts, same logic). `DriverInfo.replayOf` is an optional member; `ApiBillingRefusedError`'s second parameter is optional with the Claude default, so the previous message is byte-identical. `./export` gains `driverText`; `appReadme`'s changed signature is private. Additive throughout.
- **Gallery exporter** (`src/export/exporter.ts`, `record.ts`): every app page gains `- Driver: NAME VERSION` from `driverText(record.env.driver)`; a replay reads `DRIVER VERSION (re-graded from a recording of that run)` and never the recording path; an old replay record without `replayOf` says so. `RecordedDriver.info()` fills `replayOf` from the recording and preserves the original across a recording of a replay. The record reader (`ScenarioRunRecordSchema.env.driver`) now reads `version` and `replayOf`; note it also types `version` as `string | undefined` where the loose object accepted any value before — a narrowing of the exporter's accept set in theory, but every writer is `DriverInfo.version: string`, so no record the runner ever wrote is affected. Cosmetic: `codex --version` prints `codex-cli 0.167.0`, so a Codex page will read `- Driver: codex-cli codex-cli 0.167.0`; the Claude driver already has the same shape, so it is consistent, not wrong.
- **Key-handling contract**: external `ask` writes the Claude-shaped `mcpServers.app` config to a 0600 file inside a fresh `mkdtemp` directory, puts only `{url, configFile}` on stdin, strips the task to `StepRef` via `stepOf` (so `task.mcp.apiKey` cannot ride along), and removes the directory in `finally`. Codex writes a 0600 profile `scenario-runner-HEX.config.toml` under `$CODEX_HOME`, passes only `-p NAME`, and removes it in `finally`. Neither driver puts the key on argv, in the child environment or on stdin; the recorded turn carries `meta.process` (exit, timing, stderr tail) and the parsed answer only. The triage's ask for a test that pins "no key in any record" is met: `external-driver.test.ts` runs the real crm card through the stand-in and greps the run record, recording, scorecard and the whole gallery export for the key prefix. Residual exposure, shared with the Claude driver: a command that prints the key to stderr would land it in `stderrTail`; the README forbids that and the runner cannot prevent it.
- **Codex API-key refusal against the card's ask** ("refuse an API-key login the same way the Claude driver does"): met. `assertCodexSubscriptionLogin` refuses `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`CODEX_API_KEY` in the caller's environment, an `API key configured` status, no login, and any non-ChatGPT login (masked credential not echoed); every turn also passes `-c forced_login_method="chatgpt"`; both variables are stripped from every child. The test suite includes the dev's ablation of the guard.
- **External command: stripped but not refused when a billing variable is set.** Ask 1 asks only that keys go in a 0600 file, never on argv; the refusal rule is stated for Codex (Ask 2) and the Claude driver, whose logins the runner can read. For an arbitrary command the runner cannot see a login, so a refusal on a set variable would be a heuristic, not the Claude driver's check. Stripping the four known variables is the strongest enforceable step and the PR declares the choice in its acceptance notes. Judged acceptable against the card, not a defect; it is a maintainer policy question and is escalated in ③.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/31159-scenarios-codex-external-driver.md`: `'@objectstack/scenarios': patch`, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; the PR body carries the same two lines. No published spec schema and no governed path in the 15 files. The diff adds exports, an optional member, an optional parameter, two `--driver` values and a README section, and removes or renames no exported name (verified above), so `Clause-②: yes` is right and `patch` is the level the launch-window rule assigns. Check Changeset on the head: success.

### ③ Boundary flags

From os-dev-report 6712807610 (`open_questions: []`, `security_findings: none`, three deviations) and the PR's acceptance notes:

- Deviation 1, no assignees on `pr_create`: the order said none; the order governs the thread. Answered.
- Deviation 2, `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` not measured locally: it runs inside the Build Core job (`.github/workflows/ci.yml` line 3081), and Build Core on this head is success. Closed by CI.
- Deviation 3, Codex measured from a scratch install with no login and no model turn (proxy refuses OpenAI hosts; live runs paused per cloud#3600): acceptable under the card's own verification rule. Residual: a live `turn.completed` stream was never observed; the parser is built from `exec_events.rs` at the tag and replayed by a stand-in. The failure modes degrade to `no-result`/`turn.failed` not-measured, never a silent pass, so the first live Codex run is the remaining proof. Noted, not blocking.
- Acceptance note, external cost claim: judged in ① as acceptable. Escalated to the maintainer as a policy question: should `--driver external:` also refuse to start when `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `CODEX_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` is set in the caller's environment, as the two built-in drivers do? A one-line follow-up either way.
- Acceptance note, no served model from Codex: the scorecard already renders `model not reported (asked for …)` (`scorecard.ts` line 234) and `modelMismatch` stays unset. Answered.
- Acceptance note, a SIGKILL could leave a 0600 profile under `$CODEX_HOME`: it holds a persona key of a local dev app torn down with the run, and the file is 0600 in the user's own home. Acceptable; should-fix (non-blocking): sweep stale `scenario-runner-*.config.toml` at `CodexDriver` construction.
- Acceptance note, the e2e stand-in uses the fixture's in-memory app: the key still crosses the process boundary only via the file, which is what the pin measures. Answered.
- Acceptance note, `codex mcp list --json` holds the user's server headers in memory once: only `name` is read, nothing logged. Answered.
- Observation outside the card's asks: a Codex persona turn runs `-s read-only`, which still allows read-only shell commands, whereas the Claude driver limits a persona turn to `--allowedTools mcp__app`. The answer may therefore draw on something besides the app's MCP. Not a defect against the card; a should-fix if parity is wanted.
- Scope: all 15 files under `packages/qa/scenarios/**` plus one changeset, as the claim's file surface allows; `orchestrate.ts` untouched.

Check-runs on `fb1d76f7` at the last poll: 29 success, 13 skipped by path, 0 failure, 3 still in progress — `Test Core (1/8)`, `Test Core (2/8)`, `Test Core (3/8)`. Green and relevant: Build Core, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Type Check (workspace, source gates, consumer gates, debt ledger), Lint (ESLint, repo and tooling gates, docs and code guards, CI/release/engine gates, PM dispatch-gates, scoped tooling self-tests, scoped query-options erasure, scoped slot lookup and corpus), Test Core (4/8 to 8/8), Plan Test Core shards, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI. This verdict stands on the three in-progress Test Core shards finishing green; a failure among them re-opens it.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-mickba`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5njkh3xbcDN6EtSfw7`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT** · head `fb1d76f7d24678c01304f573d97d45a046409bf7` · card #31159 · report 6712807610 · contract review 6712878828 (PASS).

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #31159`; 15 files, +1496/-112, all under `packages/qa/scenarios/**` plus one changeset, inside the claim's file surface. `check-governed-merges --pr 31265`: NOT governed, under the 3000-line threshold.
- **Card's asks, read in the diff:**
  1. `--driver external:COMMAND`: `ExternalDriver` on the `objectstack-scenario-driver/1` contract, documented in the README. One process per call; strict JSON on stdin and stdout. A non-zero exit is `no-result(exit N)` and any other answer is `invalid-output(why)`, never an empty pass.
  2. `--driver codex`: `CodexDriver` on `codex exec --json`, with flags measured on `@openai/codex` 0.167.0. It refuses `OPENAI_API_KEY`/`CODEX_API_KEY` and any login that is not a ChatGPT login. `--model` maps to `-m`; the turn-cap flags are refused at `makeDriver` because `codex exec` has no turn cap.
  3. WorkBuddy: checked, no headless mode with structured output and an MCP client found. Per the card, no wiring and no UI bridge.
  4. The driver and version appear on the run record and on each gallery app page (`- Driver:`). A replay names its recording's driver through `replayOf`.
- **Keys (triage ⚠️):** the persona MCP key reaches either tool only in a 0600 file, removed when the turn returns, and is never on argv, in the environment or a stdin value. The end-to-end test greps the run record, recording, scorecard and full gallery export for the key and finds it in zero files. The ablation that writes the key into the record turns that test red on 7 files.
- **Public surface:** nothing previously exported from `driver.ts` or `transcript.ts` is gone (the 101 deleted lines were module-private); the new drivers are additive through `./runner`.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head: 33 success, 13 skipped (path-gated), 0 failed, 0 pending, including all eight `Test Core` shards, `Build Core` and `Check Changeset`. Local: 58 of 60 derived families exit 0. `check-plugin-teardown-shape` was re-measured at exit 0, and `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` (NOT MEASURED locally) is answered by CI's Build Core. Package suite 573/573.
- **Changeset:** `patch`, `Clause-②: yes`, `Metadata-protocol: none`; Check Changeset green.
- **Seat ruling on the review's escalated point:** an `external:` command's environment is stripped of the known billing variables but not refused when they are set. The runner cannot read an arbitrary tool's login, so a refusal would be a guess; stripping is the enforceable step, and the README says so. The seat accepts it as built; the maintainer can tighten it later.
- **Not sent back (follow-up if wanted):** the README does not yet state the `info` name grammar or the 30 s `info` timeout. A SIGKILLed Codex turn can leave a 0600 profile under `$CODEX_HOME`, as the PR itself notes. Codex `ask` runs `-s read-only`, which still allows read-only shell commands, unlike Claude's MCP-only tool list. The gallery line repeats the tool name (`codex-cli codex-cli 0.167.0`).
- **Landing:** under 「按照 pm-dispatch 规则复核过的都授权」 (2026-10-25T11:35Z) and 「你应该使用 pm-dispatch 技能审核和落地pr」 (2026-11-07T16:59Z): `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable` now.
